body.statement: What is the exact minimax expected-length frontier for replacement-private, uniformly honest intervals for \(\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\) over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\)? In particular, can the positive-density confidence-modulus handle reduce the higher-order release sensitivity while retaining the uniform bias guarantee, or can it certify that an additional nuisance-driven privacy term is unavoidable?
body.justification: The remaining gap is between the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower endpoint and the new \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper endpoint on the same full class; the higher-order achieved phase remains confined to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
body.gap: No proved coupling or stabilized higher-order full-class release decides whether the optimal privacy branch is governed by \(\gamma\), \(q\), or a private Gram.
body.consumer: A resolution would determine which privacy budget is sufficient for pointwise heterogeneous-treatment-effect inference under unknown bounded design density.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine whether a paired-microcell fuzzy family admits an \(n\)-sample coupling with sufficiently small expected Hamming cost, or construct a private stabilized higher-order estimator that improves the fixed-dimensional \(\beta\)-smooth upper on the full unknown-density class.
obligation.obstruction: The one-cell identity cancels the one-observation prior mixture but does not control dependencies caused by repeat visits to a latent microcell.  The direct full-class learner now supplies a valid upper endpoint, but its armwise local-polynomial bias is \(O(h^\beta)\), and no private higher-order Gram or propose-test-release argument has improved that endpoint on the same class.
obligation.attempted: I retained the proved Hamming-transport reduction and ordinary \(\gamma\)-bump lower, checked the paired-cell cancellation obstruction, and constructed an all-observation joint Gaussian release of both arm-specific local-polynomial Grams and moments with a spectral-floor fallback.  The resulting full-class upper closes the trivial endpoint but does not decide sharpness.
obligation.partial_result:
Define \(\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\) as the infimum, over replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private intervals with coverage at least \(1-\eta\) uniformly on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), of their worst-law mean length.  Under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), the proved results give
\[
 c\left[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}\right]
 \le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})
 \le C\left[1\wedge\left\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}
 \vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\right\}\right].
\]
The right endpoint is attained by the explicit fixed-dimensional direct-regression release using all \(n\) observations and is valid under the same full class as the lower endpoint.  Separately, the higher-order learner attains \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\) only on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), so it is not an endpoint of this full-class bracket.  The paired-cell one-observation cancellation \(uv+(1/4-u^2)t=0\) still does not control the dependence induced by repeat visits to a latent microcell in the \(n\)-sample prior mixture.  Thus the bracket is closed and nontrivial, but its sharpness and the possible \(q\)- or private-Gram branch remain unresolved.
